_note: Five scripted demo scenarios. Each step is processed by the real agent workflow. 'setup' moves vehicles before the scenario starts; 'move' moves a vehicle just before its step. Times (t) are simulated seconds.

scenarios.title: Stopped truck in fog
scenarios.summary: Vehicle A sees a stopped truck 500 m ahead in dense fog. Vehicle B confirms, Vehicle C is warned, and two later 'road clear' reports resolve the hazard.

steps.narration: Vehicle A detects a stopped truck about 500 m ahead in dense fog and sends a hazard report.

report.description: Stopped truck blocking the right lane, hazard lights on, barely visible in fog.

steps.narration: Vehicle B, in the next lane, independently confirms the same stopped truck.

report.description: Large truck stationary in the right lane.

steps.narration: Ask the Research Assistant to explain the alert.
steps.question: Why was an alert generated for Vehicle C?

steps.narration: Ask how much evidence supports the hazard.
steps.question: How many vehicles confirmed the hazard?

steps.narration: Ten minutes later, Vehicle F passes the location and reports the road is clear.

report.description: Right lane open, no truck visible.

steps.narration: Vehicle G independently reports the road is clear, which resolves the hazard.
Ask why the hazard was resolved and what was stored in long-term memory.
steps.question: Why was the hazard resolved?

scenarios.title: Road accident
scenarios.summary: A collision on I-680 southbound is confirmed by two more vehicles. Only southbound traffic behind the crash is alerted; northbound Vehicle E is not.

steps.narration: Vehicle D reports a collision about 300 m ahead on I-680 southbound.

report.description: Two-car collision blocking the left lane, debris on the road.

steps.narration: Vehicle A arrives and confirms the accident.
Vehicle B also confirms the accident, so confidence rises again.

report.description: Crashed vehicles in the left lane.

steps.narration: Ask why the confidence score increased.
steps.question: Why did the confidence score increase?

scenarios.title: Flooding
scenarios.summary: A single flooding report on a road with no history (cold start). Retrieved similar incidents raise confidence from 0.50 to 0.65, so the agent issues a verified alert instead of a caution advisory.

steps.narration: At night in heavy rain, Vehicle G reports water across both lanes under the rail bridge on Tassajara Rd, a segment with almost no recorded history.

report.description: Water across both lanes under the rail bridge underpass, heavy rain at night, depth unclear.

steps.narration: Ask the Research Assistant which past incidents influenced the decision.
steps.question: What similar incidents happened previously?

steps.narration: Vehicle A reaches the underpass and confirms the flooding.

report.description: Standing water across the road under the bridge.

steps.narration: Ask why the confidence score increased.
steps.question: Why did the confidence score increase?

scenarios.title: False hazard report
scenarios.summary: A radar-only debris report on a road with little history. Similar past radar-only reports were false, so confidence drops to 0.35 and the agent asks an approaching vehicle to look instead of alerting.

steps.narration: Vehicle H, which has radar only, reports possible debris 200 m ahead on Dougherty Rd.

report.description: Possible debris object in the right lane detected by radar only, no camera confirmation.

steps.narration: Vehicle F was asked to observe. It passes the spot with its camera and reports the road is clear.

report.description: Camera shows the right lane is clear, no debris.

steps.narration: Ask why the hazard was resolved.
steps.question: Why was the hazard resolved?

scenarios.title: Road cleared
scenarios.summary: A confirmed debris hazard on Dublin Blvd is later reported clear by two independent vehicles. The agent resolves it, sends an all-clear, and stores the outcome in long-term memory.

steps.narration: Vehicle F reports a mattress in the left lane of Dublin Blvd eastbound.

report.description: Mattress lying in the left lane, camera confirmed.

steps.narration: Vehicle B confirms the debris, so the agent issues a verified alert to Vehicle C.
Later, Vehicle D passes and reports the lane is clear.

report.description: Left lane open, nothing in the road.

steps.narration: Vehicle E independently reports the lane is clear. The hazard is resolved and an all-clear is sent.
Ask why the hazard was resolved.
steps.question: Why was the hazard resolved?

steps.narration: Ask what the agent has learned from feedback.
steps.question: What has long-term memory learned from feedback?
